newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee closes marginally higher - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee closes marginally higher - dealers.

text.p: BOMBAY, Dec 20 - The Indian rupee ended Friday marginally up against the dollar on lack of demand at 35.820/825 against the opening quotes of 35.835/845, dealers said..
"The rupee kept gaining in small amounts right through the day," said a dealer at a state-run bank..
"Even though a leading state-run bank was buying dollars, supplies were good and the rupee moved up," he added.
The rupee traded at a high of 35.825 and a low of 35.8425 per dollar on Friday, dealers said..
The Reserve Bank of India bought dollars in small lots between 35.83 to 35.825, they said..
In the forwards market, the premium on six-month dollars moved up to an annualised 8.0 percent from Thursday's 7.59 percent on covering by banks and importers, dealers added.
No further details of the bids were immediately available.
